parole.testo: Borrowed into West Semitic from Akkadian 𒀀𒂵𒈬𒌝 (agammum), from Sumerian 𒀀𒂵𒄠 (agam). Compare Classical Syriac ܐܓܡܐ (ʾaḡmā, “marsh, swamp”) and Hebrew אֲגַם (ʾaḡamm, “lake, swamp”).

parole.significato: lettuce (Lactuca gen. and Lactuca sativa in particular)
parole.testo: From Aramaic חַסָּא (ḥassā), from Akkadian 𒌑𒄭𒄑𒊬 (ḫassū, “lettuce”), from Sumerian 𒄭𒄑𒊬 (ḫi-izˢᵃʳ /⁠hiz⁠/, “lettuce”); cognates with Classical Syriac ܚ̈ܲܣܸܐ (ḥassā) and Hebrew חַסָּה (ḥássā). Note also Old Armenian հազար (hazar).

parole.significato: rope woven from palm bast or fibres
parole.testo: Ultimately from Akkadian 𒄀𒆤𒈣 (/⁠kuru⁠/, “short reed mat, collection of reeds; a woven thing”), from Sumerian 𒄥 (gur, “to twist, to wind, to turn”).
